parts.note: surface reading: odd or unusual sequences of results laid bare
setter's reading: dashing across a public place with no clothes on

explanation.surface: Some surprising runs of form have come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like winning or losing sequences; it really means running, and 'exposed' means naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaking is the prank of running naked through a public place, an unconventional way to dash about.

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one speedy aircraft or bird; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for speedy and the name of a bird famed for its aerial agility.

indicators.note: 'could be' suggests the letters may become something else once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angry rant might be aired on radio or television.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to send out or spread in all directions, much as signals are sent out.

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is to be taken away

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A fitted unit of furniture has had its top taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitted furniture' reads as one phrase, but 'Fitted' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fitted for a task is suited and capable of doing it.

clue.text: One can live on it? Barely!

definitions.text: One can live on it? Barely!

parts.words: One can live on it? Barely!
parts.note: surface reading: something that keeps a person going, though only just

parts.words: One can live on it? Barely!
parts.note: setter's reading: pay that covers only the bare necessities of life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' carries both senses: you can only just live on it, and it pays for bare essentials.
explanation.definitionFit: This is pay set at the minimum needed to buy food and shelter, enough to scrape by on.

clue.text: Tot doled out in trip? Not half!

indicators.note: 'in' places the rearranged letters inside what remains
only half of the word is wanted, so its second half goes

parts.note: taken as written, cut in half

indicators.note: 'out' suggests the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child was handed something on an outing, though only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged ODDLE sits between TR, the first half of trip, giving T-ODDLE-R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, and a toddler is a child just learning to walk.

clue.text: Indication of a good beach — no danger in sight

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: a shoreline free of rubbish or obstacles
second meaning: the idiom for the moment when nobody is watching and it is safe to proceed

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful literal reading of the idiom; the second is its usual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock idiom meaning it is safe to act because nobody threatening is around.

clue.text: Reduce power of one bet, detail being incorrect

indicators.note: letters that are incorrect are wrongly arranged and need putting right

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler's wager is weakened because some particular of it is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To debilitate is to weaken or sap the strength of something, making it feebler.

clue.text: Dish is a flop in a way

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
to flop or droop is to sag

explanation.surface: A meal turns out a failure, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a flop' looks like a verdict on the dish, but it is the word that sits inside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked dish of layered pasta sheets, sauce and filling.

clue.text: Tells stories kept back in reserve

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside the other

parts.note: RES is a common abbreviation for reserve
someone kept back is held up and so delayed

explanation.surface: Someone narrates tales that were held in store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept back' as in held behind at school, which makes you late.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate is to narrate or recount events, which is what telling stories involves.

clue.text: Nellie with bid in play can't be forgotten

indicators.note: letters in play are moved about freely into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actress named Nellie gives a memorable performance making a bid on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indelible leaves a permanent mark that cannot be erased, as a lasting memory does.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an aromatic culinary plant
second meaning: a man's first name, as Herb is

explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like the short form of Herbert, hence 'another man'; it is also the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fragrant plant used in Italian cooking and is also a common male first name.

indicators.note: 'after' sets one piece following the other in the answer

parts.note: tea is an evening or afternoon meal in Britain
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A duck remains once dinner is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left after meal' sounds like leftovers, but left is L and comes after the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater species of dabbling duck.

parts.note: surface reading: a listing of today's programmes or films
setter's reading: a small indicator lamp telling you the power or gas is running

explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' suggests 'at present', but hints at an electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small lamp or flame that stays lit to show an appliance has power or gas flowing.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: voicing one's views without fear
second meaning: talking with more volume

explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' is an adverb, read as 'speaking loudly'; the phrase means both.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both stating your views openly and raising your voice so others hear.

indicators.note: 'abroad' means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An influential official has been sent to an overseas posting.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler holding absolute authority, often exercised cruelly.

indicators.note: 'by' means beside, so one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: something fixed is set
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Benches have been installed on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Settees are long upholstered seats for two or more people, sofas.

parts.note: a ref (referee) judges a sports match
raindrops; rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: A judge abandons the lines of verse he keeps saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like a verb for the judge; it is a noun giving RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is a chorus or set of lines repeated through a song or poem.

clue.text: Quick answer in the Tripos test

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A sharp reply given in a Cambridge examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is the Cambridge University honours degree examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a swift, witty retort, originally a fencer's quick return thrust.

parts.note: surface reading: say where you have left your door keys
setter's reading: a US state whose southern tip trails off into a chain of islands called the Keys

explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like an instruction to tell, but it is a US state; the Keys are islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida Keys are a string of coral islands off that American state's southern tip.

clue.text: It's perfect and it can't change

indicators.note: 'change' is an instruction to alter the order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Something flawless that cannot be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't change' reads as a refusal, but 'change' is the instruction for the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, complete with nothing missing or broken.

clue.text: In fairness, most of the sweet stuff's belonging to us

indicators.note: 'most of' means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: candy is sweets
what belongs to us is ours

explanation.surface: In fairness, nearly all the sweets are ours.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour once meant fairness or freedom from bias; today it mostly means frankness and openness.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: distinction, being widely known
second meaning: a bulge or projection

explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a musical note or memo; here it means eminence, as in 'a person of note'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fame or importance and a part that sticks out above a surface.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A runner-up horse is a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected problem or obstacle, a hitch spoiling a plan.

clue.text: Press turns up outside UN and it's a bit sticky

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, sticky stuff

indicators.note: 'outside' puts one word around the other
in a down clue, turning a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: to press someone on is to egg them on
taken as written

explanation.surface: Journalists show up at the United Nations, where things get messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is a verb meaning to urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunge is informal British slang for a sticky, messy, unpleasant substance.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
second meaning: the main stalk of a plant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like the adjective meaning loyal; here it is the verb meaning to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check it, and a stem is the main stalk or trunk of a plant.

indicators.note: 'around' puts one word on either side of the other

parts.note: a swig is a gulp of drink
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Arrange for some alcohol to be had up north.
explanation.definitionFit: To swing something informally is to arrange or manage it, often through influence.

clue.text: A man with name as negotiator or snooper, for example

parts.note: taken as written
a gent is a man
a noun is a naming word

explanation.surface: A named man acts as a go-between or spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiator' and 'snooper' suggest a secret agent, but they are grammatical examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns formed from verbs to denote the person doing the action: one who negotiates, one who snoops.

clue.text: Test learner in drill, for instance

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, an instance

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside the other

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercise drill at school
L is the learner plate of a learner driver

explanation.surface: Assessing a trainee during practice, say.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, the school exercise class, here called drill.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a case given as an instance, which is what 'for instance' introduces.

clue.text: Pity about being in a sulk after missing round

definitions.note: pity in the old sense of ruth, regret

indicators.note: 'after' sets one piece following the other

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: 'missing' says something is absent and must be taken out

parts.note: a sulky person is morose
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry about sulking after losing a round of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth covers both compassion and sorrow for wrongdoing, so pity and regret overlap here.
